target_customer: Commercial airlines such as easyJet and VivaAerobus, and later defense and aerospace buyers of power systems
problem: Short haul commercial flights are expensive, noisy and emit carbon, and no one sold a battery electric airliner.
business_model: Development of electric aircraft and propulsion, later power systems sold to aerospace and defense customers, funded by grants and contracts
product_category: Electric aircraft and aerospace power systems

founders.name: Jeff Engler
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/CEO. Aggregator search results mention an earlier startup Podimetrics; not verified from an opened source.

founders.name: Doug Griswold
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. TechCrunch (2017-03-21) says the team had earlier received NASA funding to study electric planes.

competitors.name: Boeing and Airbus
competitors.what: Built the narrow body jets Wright Electric aimed to replace
competitors.traction_then: TechCrunch cites 967 narrow body planes sold the previous year at about 90 million dollars each

technical_complexity.rationale: A 150 to 186 seat battery electric airliner needed battery energy density, certification and propulsion beyond what existed in 2017.

defensibility.rationale: Airframe and propulsion know how and certification hurdles are hard to copy, but the whole concept depends on battery progress anyone can use.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per search coverage, the company later pivoted toward a Wright Spirit retrofit of the BAe 146 and then propulsion and power systems; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: easyJet partnered with the company in September 2017 and TechCrunch (2017-03-21) described airline interest in lower cost and zero emission short routes.

branding.domain_note: Uses weflywright.com rather than an exact name .com; no purchase detail found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Aspirational aviation pitch, Boeing for electric planes

branding.brand_signature: Boeing for electric planes tagline and the Wright 1 airliner concept
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch and trade press covered the airline partnership; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name echoes the Wright brothers and earned wide trade press coverage, but no source ties the brand to growth.

pivots.from: Wright 1 clean sheet 186 seat electric airliner
pivots.to: Wright Spirit 100 seat BAe 146 conversion and propulsion systems
pivots.why: Search coverage (Bloomberg, Aviation Week) describes the shift to a retrofit and propulsion focus; reasons not read in full

outcome_analysis: Wright Electric is still active, now selling power systems for aerospace and defense per its own site. It gained airline partners early after Y Combinator and focused on propulsion as battery limits delayed a full electric airliner. Funding information is only available from aggregators and grants, so the raise history and the strength of its outcome remain uncertain.
notes: Aggregators list a 2016 seed near 120 thousand dollars and a 3.3 million dollar FAA FAST grant or seed in 2024 with conflicting labels; single aggregator figures so no rounds are recorded. A page claiming a Series A led by BlackRock was not tied to this company. The company site currently describes aerospace and defense power systems, not only electric aircraft.
